JOEL PAUL POLIZZI
MRN: 17948266
DOB: 6/28/1986
PMD: Akhavan, Jamshid
**CC:** Rash (X1 week nose, x1 month on buttock, possible staph infection/Applied neosporin antibiotic cream/Requesting referral to allergy)
[table#1]:
| **Chief Complaint** |
| --- |
| Patient presents with |
| • | Rash |
| | | *X1 week nose, x1 month on buttock, possible staph infection*
*Applied neosporin antibiotic cream*
*Requesting referral to allergy* |
**HPI:** Joel Paul Polizzi is a 39 year old male who presents with c/o a 4 week history of a rash to the buttock and then a one-week history of a rash to the right nostril. Patient notes that he has had a single lesion on his buttock, for then in the last week or so has developed another 1-2 lesions. He has been applying topical Neosporin to both his nostril and buttock, with only somewhat relief of the nostril rash. He notes the nostril rash has a burning sensation, but he has no pain on the buttock rash. No severe pruritus. No new products. Patient has never had these symptoms before. He does not have a history of HSV. No further complaints. No drainage, nausea, vomiting, fevers, and chills.
PMHx: Past Medical History
PSHx: has a past surgical history that includes Ankle hardware implantation (Right, 03/2011); Colonoscopy (07/27/2020); and Fracture surgery (4/2009).
Meds: has a current medication list which includes the following prescription(s): clotrimazole, methimazole, mupirocin, propranolol, and sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim.
ALL: Penicillins
Review of Systems
Negative unless otherwise specified in HPI
**EXAM**
BP (!) 137/94 (BP Location: Left arm, BP Patient Position: Sitting, BP cuff size: Large) | Pulse 78 | Temp 97.9 °F (36.6 °C) (Temporal) | Resp 17 | SpO2 98%
Vital signs: mild hypertension
General: well-developed, well-nourished, nontoxic and non-ill-appearing
Neuro: no focal deficits, cognition normal, alert, speaking full sentences
Head and Face: Atraumatic, normocephalic
Eyes: sclera normal
Ears: Normal to inspection
Nose: Normal to inspection, +yellow crusting lesions right nostril, turbinates mildly erythematous
Neck: Supple
Chest: Non-labored respiration with normal expiration time
Skin: erythematous and scaling lesion (measuring 3 cm x 3 cm) on the right upper buttock with two other small erythematous lesions (5mm). No drainage. No warmth. No discharge. No streaking.
**Impression:**
[table#2]:
| | | ICD-10-CM | ICD-9-CM | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **1.** | **Staph infection ** | **B95.8** | **041.10** | **sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim (BACTRIM DS) 800-160 MG tablet** |
| | | | **mupirocin (BACTROBAN) 2 % ointment** |
| |
| 2. | Tinea | B35.9 | 110.9 | clotrimazole (LOTRIMIN) 1 % cream |
| |
**MDM:**
DDX: Hives, allergic reaction, staph infection, impetigo, HSV, folliculitis, contact dermatitis, tinea, viral exanthem, less likely abscess, cellulitis, I doubt necrotizing fasciitis, TENS, sepsis, vasculitis, meningitis, anaphylaxis
No erythroderma, skin pain, desquamation, petechiae or purpura.
Patient is well appearing, non toxic with stable vital signs complaining of a 4 week history of a rash to the buttock and then a one-week history of a rash to the right nostril. Patient notes that he has had a single lesion on his buttock, for then in the last week or so has developed another 1-2 lesions. He has been applying topical Neosporin to both his nostril and buttock, with only somewhat relief of the nostril rash. He notes the nostril rash has a burning sensation, but he has no pain on the buttock rash. No severe pruritus. No new products. Patient has never had these symptoms before. He does not have a history of HSV. On exam the patient does have a yellow crusting lesion in the right nostril, which appears likely most consistent with a staph infection. Does not appear to be secondary to HSV. Offered swab, but patient deferred. Patient
also had an erythematous and scaling lesion on the right upper buttock with 2 accompanying lesions. Possibly staph, but also could easily be tinea. Patient will take Bactrim twice daily for one-week and apply mupirocin ointment to this there. If his rash on his buttock does not improve in a couple of days with this treatment, he will then try clotrimazole.
**Plan:**
-See above
-Patient instructed to follow up with PCP within 1 week, as needed.
-Strict ER precautions reviewed. Return precautions discussed. Patient understands and agrees with the plan of care.
Ashley Castelhano, PA-C
UCSD Express Care
Supervising physician for this visit is Dr. Shauna Conry, MD
